card.occupation: Kitchen assistant at a primary school (term-time only, about 22 hours a week): food prep, serving at lunchtime, washing up and wiping down the hall afterwards
card.education_detail: Left a Gosport comprehensive at 16 in 1987 with a handful of CSEs and an O-level in English. Holds a Level 2 Food Hygiene certificate, renewed through work, and a basic first aid course done at the school a few years ago.
card.household: Lives alone in a one-bedroom first-floor housing association flat with her elderly tabby cat, Biscuit. Her younger sister Michelle lives about ten minutes away in Bridgemary and they see each other most weekends.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and brought up in Gosport. Her dad worked in the dockyard and her mum did cleaning jobs. Not religious, though she went to Sunday school as a child and still likes a carol service at Christmas. Firmly local: she has lived within a couple of miles of where she grew up nearly all her life.
card.professional_persona: Reliable and quietly proud of her work. She has been at the same school for eleven years and before that did shop work and cleaning. She is always early, keeps the kitchen spotless and knows which children have allergies or won't eat peas. The cook relies on her. She would never call in sick unless she really couldn't stand, and that has happened more often lately because of her knees and back. She worries she is letting people down.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. Her arthritis and asthma make anything strenuous hard. She tries to do short walks along the seafront at Stokes Bay when the weather's kind. She watches a bit of Wimbledon and has a soft spot for Pompey because her dad supported them, but she doesn't follow the matches closely.
card.arts_persona: Likes what she likes: Saturday-night telly, quiz shows like The Chase and Pointless, crime dramas, and Strictly with her sister on the phone. She reads library paperbacks, mostly cosy mysteries and family sagas. She once went to see a musical in Southampton for Michelle's fiftieth and still talks about it.
card.travel_persona: Doesn't travel much, partly money and partly worry. She has been abroad once, to Benidorm with friends at 24. Holidays now mean a week in a static caravan in Devon or Dorset with her sister, or a day trip to the Isle of Wight on the ferry. She gets anxious about trains and connections and likes things planned well in advance.
card.culinary_persona: Plain home cooking on a budget: shepherd's pie, sausage casserole, jacket potatoes, soup made in batches and frozen in portions. She calls her evening meal dinner. She is careful with her money at the big Asda and looks out for yellow-sticker reductions. Her treat is fish and chips on a Friday, or a Victoria sponge she bakes herself when someone has a birthday.
hobbies_and_interests: Crocheting small blankets and hats for the neonatal unit at Queen Alexandra Hospital
Feeding the birds from her little balcony
Browsing charity shops in the high street
Watching quiz shows and crime dramas
skills: Food prep and safe food handling
Keeping a kitchen clean and organised to inspection standard
Remembering everyone's birthdays and dietary needs
card.career_goals: Mainly to keep going at the school as long as her body lets her and not have to give it up before state pension age. She has wondered about dropping her hours or asking for a role with less standing, but she worries about the money. She has no big ambitions; she would just like to feel less worn out and to stop worrying about being let go.
card.voice: Soft, friendly southern English accent with mild Hampshire/Portsmouth colour, nothing broad. Moderate pace, sometimes speeding up when she's nervous and then apologising. Uses 'erm' quite a lot when thinking, 'sort of' and 'you know' as softeners, and the odd 'you was' in casual speech. Says 'sorry' a lot, both to apologise and to ask for a question again ('sorry, what was that, love?'). Calls people 'love' now and then. She hates silence and will fill it with 'I don't know if that's what you wanted' or a little laugh. She checks she's answered properly and says thank you more than once at the end.
card.typing: Types slowly with one or two fingers on her phone. Usually starts with a capital because the phone does it, but punctuation is light: commas instead of full stops, sometimes no full stop at the end. Apostrophes are hit and miss ('dont', 'its', but 'I'm' when autocorrect catches it). Few abbreviations apart from 'tv' and 'etc'. She tends to add a polite extra line like 'hope that helps' or 'sorry if this isnt right'.
card.with_strangers: Warm, eager to please and a bit nervous at first. She worries she will say the wrong thing or that her answers aren't interesting enough. She is very agreeable and finds it hard to disagree outright, so she softens any criticism heavily. Once she relaxes she is chatty and kind, asks how the other person is doing, and will happily talk about her cat or the kids at school.
small_things: The price of everything at Asda going up again
Biscuit the cat being fussy about his food
The kids at school and what they will and won't eat
Her latest jigsaw being 'a nightmare, all sky'
Her knees playing up on cold mornings
What she watched on telly last night
The ferry to Portsmouth being late again
deeper_things: Her arthritis and asthma are getting worse and she is frightened of not being able to work
She sometimes feels lonely in the evenings and the cat is a big comfort
Her mum died four years ago after a long illness and Joanne did most of the caring
She had a long relationship in her thirties that ended, and she quietly regrets never having children
She worries about money every month and has used the food bank once, which she felt ashamed about
She has been on medication for anxiety on and off since her forties
card.webcam_photo: Taken from a phone propped against something on a table, angled slightly upwards, so her chin and the ceiling are a little more visible than ideal. Lighting comes mainly from a window to her left, giving soft daylight on one side of her face, with the other side slightly shadowed. She is a woman in her mid-fifties with a round, kind face, fair skin with some redness on the cheeks and fine lines around the eyes. Her shoulder-length hair is mid-brown with visible grey at the roots, tucked behind her ears. She is smiling a little uncertainly, mouth closed, eyebrows slightly raised as if checking the camera is working. She wears thin gold-rimmed reading glasses and a lilac fleece zipped halfway over a plain white T-shirt. Behind her is a magnolia-painted wall with a framed print of a lighthouse, a small wooden shelf with a few paperbacks, a photo frame and a china cat ornament. Part of a beige settee with a crocheted blanket in pastel squares is visible to the right, along with the edge of a radiator with a tea towel drying on it.
